steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Thermoplastics soften when heated and harden when cooled; they can be repeatedly reshaped (e.g. ABS, acrylic, nylon, polycarbonate, polypropylene). | Key Fact: Thermosetting polymers undergo an irreversible chemical change when heated; they cannot be remelted (e.g. epoxy resin, melamine formaldehyde, polyester resin). | Key Fact: Elastomers are polymers with elastic properties; vulcanised rubber is the most common engineering elastomer. | Key Fact: ABS is tough, impact-resistant and easily injection-moulded; used for enclosures, car interiors and consumer products.
